"""Score a results file against a reference results file with the brief's three checks.

    python compare.py reference.jsonl candidate.jsonl

Exits 1 when the candidate fails any threshold.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from typing import TypedDict

F1_THRESHOLD = 0.95
EXACT_THRESHOLD = 0.85
WITHIN_ONE_THRESHOLD = 0.95

SecondKey = tuple[str, int]


class Second(TypedDict):
    objects: frozenset[str]
    people: int


def load(path: str) -> tuple[dict[SecondKey, Second], set[str]]:
    seconds: dict[SecondKey, Second] = {}
    errors: set[str] = set()
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            row = json.loads(line)
            if "error" in row:
                errors.add(row["video"])
            else:
                seconds[(row["video"], row["second"])] = {"objects": frozenset(row["objects"]), "people": row["people"]}
    return seconds, errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("reference")
    parser.add_argument("candidate")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    ref, ref_errors = load(args.reference)
    cand, cand_errors = load(args.candidate)
    if not ref:
        print("reference has no seconds")
        return 1

    tp = fp = fn = exact = within_one = 0
    for key, r in ref.items():
        c = cand.get(key)
        objects = c["objects"] if c else frozenset[str]()
        tp += len(r["objects"] & objects)
        fn += len(r["objects"] - objects)
        fp += len(objects - r["objects"])
        if c is not None:
            exact += c["people"] == r["people"]
            within_one += abs(c["people"] - r["people"]) <= 1
    extra = cand.keys() - ref.keys()
    fp += sum(len(cand[k]["objects"]) for k in extra)

    f1 = 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn) if tp + fp + fn else 1.0
    exact_rate = exact / len(ref)
    within_rate = within_one / len(ref)
    passed = f1 >= F1_THRESHOLD and exact_rate >= EXACT_THRESHOLD and within_rate >= WITHIN_ONE_THRESHOLD

    print(f"seconds: reference {len(ref)}, candidate {len(cand)}, missing {len(ref.keys() - cand.keys())}, extra {len(extra)}")
    print(f"errors: reference {sorted(ref_errors)}, candidate {sorted(cand_errors)}")
    print(f"objects F1:        {f1:.4f}  (tp {tp}, fp {fp}, fn {fn}, need >= {F1_THRESHOLD})")
    print(f"people exact:      {exact_rate:.4f}  (need >= {EXACT_THRESHOLD})")
    print(f"people within 1:   {within_rate:.4f}  (need >= {WITHIN_ONE_THRESHOLD})")
    print("PASS" if passed else "FAIL")
    return 0 if passed else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

batches frames (across seconds of the same video) through YOLO and writes one JSON line per second.

import argparse
import io
import json
import os
import queue
import statistics
import threading
from collections import Counter
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from time import time
from typing import TextIO

import av
import numpy as np
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import torch
from av.video.frame import VideoFrame
from numpy.typing import NDArray
from ultralytics import YOLO

PT_MODEL_FILE = "yolo/yolo11l.pt"
ENGINE_MODEL_FILE = "yolo/yolo11l.engine"  # built by build_engine.py
MODEL_INPUT_SIZE = 640
MODEL_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.4
OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES = ("person", "car", "dog", "laptop", "cell phone")
# Frames per model call. The TensorRT engine is built with this as its max batch, so keep them in sync.
BATCH_SIZE = 64
QUEUE_SIZE = 4 * BATCH_SIZE  # decoded frames buffered ahead of the model
ERROR_MESSAGE = "could not decode video"

Image = NDArray[np.uint8]

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DecodedFrame:
    video: str
    second: int
    image: Image


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SecondEnd:
    video: str
    second: int
    frame_count: int


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class VideoFailed:
    video: str

class DecodingDone:
    crash: BaseException | None = None  # set if the decoder thread itself died

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        return "0"
    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        return "mps"
    return "cpu"

    return ENGINE_MODEL_FILE if device == "0" and os.path.exists(ENGINE_MODEL_FILE) else PT_MODEL_FILE

    def __init__(self, model_file: str, device: str):
        self.device = device
        self.model = YOLO(model_file, task="detect")
        names: dict[int, str] = self.model.names

            raise ValueError(f"Classes {missing} not found in the model's class names.")

        self.class_ids = [name_to_id[name] for name in OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES]

    def predict(self, images: list[Image]) -> list[tuple[set[str], int]]:
        """Return (objects found, people count) for each image."""
        results = self.model.predict(images,
                                     imgsz=MODEL_INPUT_SIZE,
                                     conf=MODEL_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD,
                                     classes=self.class_ids,
                                     quantize=16 if self.device == "0" else None,  # FP16 on CUDA only
                                     batch=BATCH_SIZE,
                                     verbose=False,
                                     device=self.device)

    """Yield (second, image) per frame, and (second, None) once each second is complete, empty seconds included.

class ResultWriter:
    """Aggregates per-frame detections into per-second lines, writing each second once all its frames are in."""

    def __init__(self, out: TextIO):
        self.out = out
        self.pending: dict[tuple[str, int], SecondStats] = {}

    def _write(self, line: dict[str, object]) -> None:
        self.out.write(json.dumps(line) + "\n")

    def add_detections(self, frames: list[DecodedFrame], detections: list[tuple[set[str], int]]) -> None:
        touched: set[tuple[str, int]] = set()

            self._write_if_complete(key)

    def end_second(self, event: SecondEnd) -> None:
        key = (event.video, event.second)
        self.pending.setdefault(key, SecondStats()).frame_count = event.frame_count
        self._write_if_complete(key)

    def _write_if_complete(self, key: tuple[str, int]) -> None:
        stats = self.pending[key]
        if stats.frame_count is None or stats.frames_done < stats.frame_count:
            return
        del self.pending[key]
        n = stats.frame_count
        objects = [name for name in OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES if n and stats.object_frames[name] >= n / 2]
        people = int(statistics.median(stats.people)) if stats.people else 0  # int() rounds a .5 median down
        self._write({"video": key[0], "second": key[1], "objects": objects, "people": people})

    def fail_video(self, video: str) -> None:
        """Drop the unfinished seconds of a failed video and write its error line. Call after flushing the batch."""
        for key in [k for k in self.pending if k[0] == video]:
            del self.pending[key]
        self._write({"video": video, "error": ERROR_MESSAGE})


def run(parquet_files: list[str], output_file: str, predictor: Predictor, max_rows: int) -> None:
    events: queue.Queue[Event] = queue.Queue(maxsize=QUEUE_SIZE)
    decoder = threading.Thread(target=decode_all, args=(parquet_files, max_rows, events), daemon=True)
    decoder.start()

    with open(output_file, "w") as out:
        writer = ResultWriter(out)
        batch: list[DecodedFrame] = []

        def flush() -> None:
            if batch:
                writer.add_detections(batch, predictor.predict([f.image for f in batch]))
                batch.clear()

        while True:
            event = events.get()
            match event:
                case DecodedFrame():
                    # Same-shape batches keep Ultralytics' minimal letterbox, matching single-video inference.
                    if batch and batch[0].image.shape != event.image.shape:
                        flush()
                    batch.append(event)
                    if len(batch) >= BATCH_SIZE:
                        flush()
                case SecondEnd():
                    writer.end_second(event)
                case VideoFailed():
                    flush()
                    writer.fail_video(event.video)
                case DecodingDone(crash=crash):
                    flush()
                    if crash is not None:
                        raise crash
                    break
    decoder.join()


def get_parquet_files(folder_path: str, max_files: int) -> list[str]:
    files = sorted(os.path.join(folder_path, f) for f in os.listdir(folder_path) if f.endswith(".parquet"))
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No Parquet files found in the folder: {folder_path}")
    return files[:max_files] if max_files > 0 else files


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="YOLO11l Object Detection on FineVideo Parquet Files")
    parser.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="Folder containing .parquet files")
    parser.add_argument("--output", default="results.jsonl", help="jsonl file to write the results to")
    parser.add_argument("--model", help=f"YOLO model file (default: {ENGINE_MODEL_FILE} on CUDA if built, else {PT_MODEL_FILE})")
    parser.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=0, help="Only process this many parquet files (0 = all)")
    parser.add_argument("--max-rows", type=int, default=0, help="Only process this many videos per file (0 = all)")
    parser.add_argument("--dev", action="store_true", help="Shortcut for --max-files 1 --max-rows 1")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.dev:
        args.max_files, args.max_rows = 1, 1

    device = pick_device()
    model_file: str = args.model or default_model(device)
    print(f"Using {model_file} on device {device}")
    predictor = Predictor(model_file, device)
    run(get_parquet_files(args.input, args.max_files), args.output, predictor, args.max_rows)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_time = time()
    main()
    print(f"Total processing time: {time() - start_time:.2f} seconds")

"""YOLO11l object detection over every second of every video in a folder of FineVideo Parquet files.

    python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl

A background thread decodes videos into BGR frames and pushes them onto a bounded queue. The main thread
batches frames (across seconds of the same video) through YOLO and writes one JSON line per second.
"""
import argparse
import io
import json
import os
import queue
import statistics
import threading
from collections import Counter
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from time import time
from typing import TextIO

import av
import numpy as np
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import torch
from av.video.frame import VideoFrame
from numpy.typing import NDArray
from ultralytics import YOLO

PT_MODEL_FILE = "yolo/yolo11l.pt"
ENGINE_MODEL_FILE = "yolo/yolo11l.engine"  # built by build_engine.py
MODEL_INPUT_SIZE = 640
MODEL_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.4
OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES = ("person", "car", "dog", "laptop", "cell phone")
# Frames per model call. The TensorRT engine is built with this as its max batch, so keep them in sync.
BATCH_SIZE = 64
QUEUE_SIZE = 4 * BATCH_SIZE  # decoded frames buffered ahead of the model
ERROR_MESSAGE = "could not decode video"

Image = NDArray[np.uint8]


# Events sent from the decoder thread to the main thread, in decode order.
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DecodedFrame:
    video: str
    second: int
    image: Image


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SecondEnd:
    video: str
    second: int
    frame_count: int


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class VideoFailed:
    video: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DecodingDone:
    crash: BaseException | None = None  # set if the decoder thread itself died


Event = DecodedFrame | SecondEnd | VideoFailed | DecodingDone


def pick_device() -> str:
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        return "0"
    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        return "mps"
    return "cpu"


def default_model(device: str) -> str:
    return ENGINE_MODEL_FILE if device == "0" and os.path.exists(ENGINE_MODEL_FILE) else PT_MODEL_FILE


class Predictor:
    def __init__(self, model_file: str, device: str):
        self.device = device
        self.model = YOLO(model_file, task="detect")
        names: dict[int, str] = self.model.names
        name_to_id = {name: class_id for class_id, name in names.items()}
        missing = [name for name in OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES if name not in name_to_id]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"Classes {missing} not found in the model's class names.")
        self.names = names
        self.class_ids = [name_to_id[name] for name in OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES]

    def predict(self, images: list[Image]) -> list[tuple[set[str], int]]:
        """Return (objects found, people count) for each image."""
        results = self.model.predict(images,
                                     imgsz=MODEL_INPUT_SIZE,
                                     conf=MODEL_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD,
                                     classes=self.class_ids,
                                     quantize=16 if self.device == "0" else None,  # FP16 on CUDA only
                                     batch=BATCH_SIZE,
                                     verbose=False,
                                     device=self.device)
        detections: list[tuple[set[str], int]] = []
        for result in results:
            class_ids: list[int] = result.boxes.cls.int().tolist() if result.boxes is not None else []
            names = [self.names[class_id] for class_id in class_ids]
            detections.append((set(names), names.count("person")))
        return detections


def to_bgr(frame: VideoFrame) -> Image:
    """BGR array with the display-matrix rotation applied (frame.rotation is counter-clockwise degrees)."""
    image: Image = frame.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
    k = (frame.rotation // 90) % 4
    return np.ascontiguousarray(np.rot90(image, k=k)) if k else image


def decode_video(video_bytes: bytes) -> Iterator[tuple[int, Image | None]]:
    """Yield (second, image) per frame, and (second, None) once each second is complete, empty seconds included.
    A frame's second is floor((pts - first_pts) * time_base), i.e. counted from the first decoded frame."""
    with av.open(io.BytesIO(video_bytes), mode="r") as container:
        stream = container.streams.video[0]
        stream.thread_type = "AUTO"
        first_pts: int | None = None
        current_second = 0
        for frame in container.decode(stream):
            if frame.pts is None:
                raise ValueError("frame without timestamp")
            if first_pts is None:
                first_pts = frame.pts
            # shortcut: out-of-order timestamps are folded into the current second
            second = max(int((frame.pts - first_pts) * frame.time_base), current_second)
            while second > current_second:
                yield current_second, None
                current_second += 1
            yield second, to_bgr(frame)
        if first_pts is None:
            raise ValueError("no frames decoded")
        yield current_second, None


def iter_videos(parquet_file: str, max_rows: int) -> Iterator[tuple[int, bytes]]:
    """Yield (row index, mp4 bytes), one row at a time so a whole file never sits in memory."""
    batches = pq.ParquetFile(parquet_file).iter_batches(batch_size=1, columns=["mp4"])
    for row_index, batch in enumerate(batches):
        if 0 < max_rows <= row_index:
            return
        video_bytes: bytes = batch.column(0)[0].as_py()
        yield row_index, video_bytes


def decode_all(parquet_files: list[str], max_rows: int, events: "queue.Queue[Event]") -> None:
    """Decoder thread: turn every video into events. Never lets an exception escape."""
    try:
        for parquet_file in parquet_files:
            name = os.path.basename(parquet_file)
            row_index = 0
            try:
                for row_index, video_bytes in iter_videos(parquet_file, max_rows):
                    video = f"{name}:{row_index}"
                    print(f"Decoding {video}")
                    frame_count = 0
                    try:
                        for second, image in decode_video(video_bytes):
                            if image is None:
                                events.put(SecondEnd(video, second, frame_count))
                                frame_count = 0
                            else:
                                events.put(DecodedFrame(video, second, image))
                                frame_count += 1
                    except Exception as e:
                        print(f"Error decoding {video}: {e}")
                        events.put(VideoFailed(video))
            except Exception as e:  # unreadable or damaged parquet file: blame the row we were on
                print(f"Error reading {parquet_file}: {e}")
                events.put(VideoFailed(f"{name}:{row_index}"))
        events.put(DecodingDone())
    except BaseException as e:
        events.put(DecodingDone(crash=e))


@dataclass(slots=True)
class SecondStats:
    frames_done: int = 0
    frame_count: int | None = None  # known once the decoder has finished the second
    object_frames: Counter[str] = field(default_factory=Counter[str])
    people: list[int] = field(default_factory=list[int])


class ResultWriter:
    """Aggregates per-frame detections into per-second lines, writing each second once all its frames are in."""

    def __init__(self, out: TextIO):
        self.out = out
        self.pending: dict[tuple[str, int], SecondStats] = {}

    def _write(self, line: dict[str, object]) -> None:
        self.out.write(json.dumps(line) + "\n")

    def add_detections(self, frames: list[DecodedFrame], detections: list[tuple[set[str], int]]) -> None:
        touched: set[tuple[str, int]] = set()
        for frame, (objects, people) in zip(frames, detections, strict=True):
            key = (frame.video, frame.second)
            stats = self.pending.setdefault(key, SecondStats())
            stats.frames_done += 1
            stats.object_frames.update(objects)
            stats.people.append(people)
            touched.add(key)
        for key in touched:
            self._write_if_complete(key)

    def end_second(self, event: SecondEnd) -> None:
        key = (event.video, event.second)
        self.pending.setdefault(key, SecondStats()).frame_count = event.frame_count
        self._write_if_complete(key)

    def _write_if_complete(self, key: tuple[str, int]) -> None:
        stats = self.pending[key]
        if stats.frame_count is None or stats.frames_done < stats.frame_count:
            return
        del self.pending[key]
        n = stats.frame_count
        objects = [name for name in OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES if n and stats.object_frames[name] >= n / 2]
        people = int(statistics.median(stats.people)) if stats.people else 0  # int() rounds a .5 median down
        self._write({"video": key[0], "second": key[1], "objects": objects, "people": people})

    def fail_video(self, video: str) -> None:
        """Drop the unfinished seconds of a failed video and write its error line. Call after flushing the batch."""
        for key in [k for k in self.pending if k[0] == video]:
            del self.pending[key]
        self._write({"video": video, "error": ERROR_MESSAGE})


def run(parquet_files: list[str], output_file: str, predictor: Predictor, max_rows: int) -> None:
    events: queue.Queue[Event] = queue.Queue(maxsize=QUEUE_SIZE)
    decoder = threading.Thread(target=decode_all, args=(parquet_files, max_rows, events), daemon=True)
    decoder.start()

    with open(output_file, "w") as out:
        writer = ResultWriter(out)
        batch: list[DecodedFrame] = []

        def flush() -> None:
            if batch:
                writer.add_detections(batch, predictor.predict([f.image for f in batch]))
                batch.clear()

        while True:
            event = events.get()
            match event:
                case DecodedFrame():
                    # Same-shape batches keep Ultralytics' minimal letterbox, matching single-video inference.
                    if batch and batch[0].image.shape != event.image.shape:
                        flush()
                    batch.append(event)
                    if len(batch) >= BATCH_SIZE:
                        flush()
                case SecondEnd():
                    writer.end_second(event)
                case VideoFailed():
                    flush()
                    writer.fail_video(event.video)
                case DecodingDone(crash=crash):
                    flush()
                    if crash is not None:
                        raise crash
                    break
    decoder.join()


def get_parquet_files(folder_path: str, max_files: int) -> list[str]:
    files = sorted(os.path.join(folder_path, f) for f in os.listdir(folder_path) if f.endswith(".parquet"))
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No Parquet files found in the folder: {folder_path}")
    return files[:max_files] if max_files > 0 else files


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="YOLO11l Object Detection on FineVideo Parquet Files")
    parser.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="Folder containing .parquet files")
    parser.add_argument("--output", default="results.jsonl", help="jsonl file to write the results to")
    parser.add_argument("--model", help=f"YOLO model file (default: {ENGINE_MODEL_FILE} on CUDA if built, else {PT_MODEL_FILE})")
    parser.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=0, help="Only process this many parquet files (0 = all)")
    parser.add_argument("--max-rows", type=int, default=0, help="Only process this many videos per file (0 = all)")
    parser.add_argument("--dev", action="store_true", help="Shortcut for --max-files 1 --max-rows 1")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.dev:
        args.max_files, args.max_rows = 1, 1

    device = pick_device()
    model_file: str = args.model or default_model(device)
    print(f"Using {model_file} on device {device}")
    predictor = Predictor(model_file, device)
    run(get_parquet_files(args.input, args.max_files), args.output, predictor, args.max_rows)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_time = time()
    main()
    print(f"Total processing time: {time() - start_time:.2f} seconds")

from time import time
from ultralytics import YOLO
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import numpy as np
import argparse
import os
import io
import av
import json
import statistics
import torch

from av.video.frame import VideoFrame

MODEL_FILE: str = "yolo/yolo11l.pt"
MODEL_INPUT_SIZE: int = 640
MODEL_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: float = 0.4
OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES: list = ["person", "car", "dog", "laptop", "cell phone"]

# Production settings
MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS: int = -1
ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE: int = -1
SHOW_VERBOSE_PREDICTIONS: bool = False
SAVE_FRAMES: bool = False

# Development settings
DEV_MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS: int = 1
DEV_ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE: int = 1
DEV_SHOW_VERBOSE_PREDICTIONS: bool = False
DEV_SAVE_FRAMES: bool = False

class Predictor:
    def __init__(self, model_file: str, input_size: int, confidence_threshold: float, class_names: list[str]):
        self.input_size = input_size
        self.confidence_threshold = confidence_threshold
        self.class_names = class_names
        self._load_model(model_file)
        self.class_ids = self._get_class_ids(class_names)

    def _load_model(self, model_file: str):
        self.device = "cpu"
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            self.device = "0"
        if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
            self.device = "mps"

        self.model = YOLO(model_file)

    def _get_class_ids(self, class_names: list[str]) -> list[int]:
        class_ids = []
        for class_name in class_names:
            if class_name in self.model.names.values():
                class_id = list(self.model.names.keys())[list(self.model.names.values()).index(class_name)]
                class_ids.append(class_id)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Class name '{class_name}' not found in the model's class names.")
        return class_ids

    @staticmethod
    def _to_bgr(frame: VideoFrame) -> np.ndarray:
        """BGR array with the display-matrix rotation applied (frame.rotation is counter-clockwise degrees)."""
        image = frame.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
        k = (frame.rotation // 90) % 4
        return np.ascontiguousarray(np.rot90(image, k=k)) if k else image

    def predict(self, frames: list[VideoFrame]):
        return self.model.predict([self._to_bgr(f) for f in frames],
                                  imgsz=self.input_size,
                                  conf=self.confidence_threshold,
                                  classes=self.class_ids,
                                  quantize=16 if self.device == "0" else None,  # FP16 on CUDA only
                                  verbose=SHOW_VERBOSE_PREDICTIONS,
                                  device=self.device)

    def evaluate(self, result) -> tuple[set[str], int]:
        unique_objects = set()
        people_count = 0
        for box in result.boxes:
            class_id = int(box.cls[0])
            class_name = self.model.names[class_id]
            unique_objects.add(class_name)
            if class_name == "person":
                people_count += 1
        return unique_objects, people_count

def get_parquet_files(folder_path: str) -> list[str]:
    """Get a list of all Parquet files in the specified folder."""
    files = sorted([os.path.join(folder_path, f) for f in os.listdir(folder_path) if f.endswith(".parquet")])
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No Parquet files found in the folder: {folder_path}")
    if MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS > 0 and len(files) > MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS:
        print(f"Limiting to {MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS} files for processing.")
        files = files[:MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS]
    return files
class Logger:
    def __init__(self, output_file: str):
        self.output_file = output_file
        open(output_file, "w").close()  # start fresh so reruns don't duplicate lines

    def _append(self, file: str, row_index: int, data: dict):
        file_name = os.path.basename(file)
        data["video"] = f"{file_name}:{row_index}"
        with open(self.output_file, 'a') as f:
            json.dump(data, f)
            f.write('\n')

    def log_error(self, file: str, row_index: int):
        self._append(file, row_index, {"error": "could not decode video"})

    def log_second(self, file: str, row_index: int, second: int, objects: list[str], people: int):
        self._append(file, row_index, {"second": second, "objects": objects, "people": people})

class VideoProcessor:
    def __init__(self, predictor: Predictor, logger: Logger, video: bytes, file: str, row: int):
        self.predictor = predictor
        self.logger = logger
        self.video_bytes = video
        self.file = file
        self.row = row

    def _save_frame(self, frame: VideoFrame, second: int, frame_index: int):
        if not SAVE_FRAMES:
            return
        output_dir = f"frames/{os.path.basename(self.file)}/row_{self.row}"
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        frame.save(os.path.join(output_dir, f"second_{second}_frame_{frame_index}.jpg"))

    def _frames_by_second(self):
        """Decode the video once and yield (second, frames) for every second, including empty ones.
        A frame's second is floor((pts - first_pts) * time_base), i.e. counted from the first decoded frame."""
        with av.open(io.BytesIO(self.video_bytes), mode="r") as container:
            stream = container.streams.video[0]
            stream.thread_type = "AUTO"
            first_pts = None
            current_second, frames = 0, []
            for frame_index, frame in enumerate(container.decode(stream)):
                if frame.pts is None:
                    raise ValueError("frame without timestamp")
                if first_pts is None:
                    first_pts = frame.pts
                # ponytail: out-of-order timestamps are folded into the current second
                second = max(int((frame.pts - first_pts) * frame.time_base), current_second)
                while second > current_second:
                    yield current_second, frames
                    current_second, frames = current_second + 1, []
                frames.append(frame)
                self._save_frame(frame, second, frame_index)
            if first_pts is None:
                raise ValueError("no frames decoded")
            yield current_second, frames

    def _process_second(self, second: int, frames: list[VideoFrame]):
        item_counts = {x: 0 for x in OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES}
        people_counts = []
        for result in self.predictor.predict(frames) if frames else []:
            unique_objects, people_count = self.predictor.evaluate(result)
            for obj in unique_objects:
                item_counts[obj] += 1
            people_counts.append(people_count)

        people = int(statistics.median(people_counts)) if people_counts else 0
        objects_detected = [obj for obj, count in item_counts.items() if frames and count >= len(frames) / 2]
        self.logger.log_second(self.file, self.row, second, objects_detected, people)

    def process(self):
        print(f"Processing video from file: {self.file}, row: {self.row}")
        for second, frames in self._frames_by_second():
            self._process_second(second, frames)

class ParquetProcessor:
    def __init__(self, predictor: Predictor, logger: Logger, file_path: str):
        self.predictor = predictor
        self.logger = logger
        self.file_path = file_path
        self.table = pq.read_table(file_path, columns=["mp4"])

    def _get_mp4_count(self) -> int:
        if ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE > 0 and self.table.num_rows > ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE:
            print(f"Limiting to {ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE} mp4s for processing.")
            return ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE
        return self.table.num_rows

    def process(self):
        mp4_column = self.table.column("mp4")
        for row_index in range(self._get_mp4_count()):
            try:
                video_bytes = mp4_column[row_index].as_py()
                VideoProcessor(self.predictor, self.logger, video_bytes, self.file_path, row_index).process()
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.log_error(self.file_path, row_index)
                print(f"Error processing row {row_index}: {e}")

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="YOLO11l Object Detection on FineVideo Parquet Files")
    parser.add_argument("--input", type=str, required=True, help="Folder containing .parquet files")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=str, default="results.jsonl", help="jsonl file to write the results to")
    parser.add_argument("--model", type=str, default=MODEL_FILE, help="Path to the YOLO model file")
    parser.add_argument("--dev", action="store_true", help="Run in development mode with limited files and rows for testing")

    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.dev:
        global MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS, ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE, SHOW_VERBOSE_PREDICTIONS, SAVE_FRAMES
        MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS = DEV_MAX_FILES_TO_PROCESS
        ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE = DEV_ROWS_TO_PROCESS_PER_FILE
        SHOW_VERBOSE_PREDICTIONS = DEV_SHOW_VERBOSE_PREDICTIONS
        SAVE_FRAMES = DEV_SAVE_FRAMES

    input_folder = args.input
    output_file = args.output
    predictor = Predictor(args.model, MODEL_INPUT_SIZE, MODEL_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, OBJECT_DETECTION_CLASSES)

    parquet_files = get_parquet_files(input_folder)
    logger = Logger(output_file)

    for file_path in parquet_files:
        try:
            parquet_processor = ParquetProcessor(predictor, logger, file_path)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.log_error(file_path, 0)
            print(f"Error reading parquet file {file_path}: {e}")
            continue
        parquet_processor.process()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_time = time()
    main()
    end_time = time()
    print(f"Total processing time: {end_time - start_time:.2f} seconds")

"""Build the TensorRT FP16 engine that run.py uses on CUDA.

    python build_engine.py

Run once on the machine that will run run.py: TensorRT engines only work on the GPU and TensorRT version they
were built with. Needs an NVIDIA GPU and yolo/yolo11l.pt (see README).
"""
import os

import torch
from ultralytics import YOLO

from run import BATCH_SIZE, ENGINE_MODEL_FILE, MODEL_INPUT_SIZE, PT_MODEL_FILE


def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise SystemExit("TensorRT export needs a CUDA GPU.")
    exported = YOLO(PT_MODEL_FILE, task="detect").export(
        format="engine",
        imgsz=MODEL_INPUT_SIZE,
        quantize=16,  # FP16
        # Dynamic shapes keep Ultralytics' minimal letterbox (e.g. 384x640 for 16:9), exactly as with the .pt model.
        # A static engine would pad every frame to 640x640 and drift from the reference results.
        dynamic=True,
        batch=BATCH_SIZE,  # max batch of the optimisation profile; run.py never sends more
        simplify=False,  # TensorRT fuses the graph itself; skips the onnxslim/onnxruntime dependencies
        device=0,
    )
    if os.path.abspath(str(exported)) != os.path.abspath(ENGINE_MODEL_FILE):
        raise SystemExit(f"Engine written to {exported}, expected {ENGINE_MODEL_FILE}")
    print(f"Built {ENGINE_MODEL_FILE}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

17	```

20

23	```
24	
25	## Output Format
26	
27	```jsonl
28	{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 12, "objects": ["person", "laptop"], "people":
29	2}
30	{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 13, "objects": [], "people": 0}
31	{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:5", "error": "could not decode video"}
32	```
33	
34	- `video` is the Parquet file name without its folder, a colon, and the row number in that file, counting from 0.
35	- Second 12 holds the frames whose timestamp is at least 12.0 and below 13.0 seconds, counted from the first decoded frame of the video.
36	- There is a line for every second up to and including the second that holds the last frame. A second with nothing found has an empty list and "people": 0.
37	- Object names are exactly `person, car, dog, laptop, cell phone`. They are irrespective of order.
38	- If a video can't be processed at any point, there exists an error message `could not decode video`. earlier seconds are already logged, after failure that video is aborted.
39	
40	## Detection Criteria
41	
42	- An object is present in a second if the model finds it in at least half of that second's frames.
43	- The people count for a second is the median of the number of people found in each frame of that second, rounded down when it falls halfway between two numbers.

50	- The test set is about 13 hours of FineVideo video in the same Parquet format, Some test files may be damaged or unusual. # YOLO11l Object Detection in HuggingFace FineVideo Dataset for Alethia AI Take Home Assignment

- Dataset: `data/train-00000-of-01357.parquet` to `data/train-00001-of-01357.parquet` of [FineVideo](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFV/finevideo)
- Detection Model: Ultralytics YOLO11l specifically [yolo11l.pt](https://huggingface.co/Ultralytics/YOLO11/blob/main/yolo11l.pt), download in the preparatory commands.
- Assignment details in AI_Engineering_TakeHome_Brief.pdf

## Installing requirements

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Preparatory Commands

```sh
hf download hf://Ultralytics/YOLO11@bee92e2/yolo11l.pt --local-dir yolo
```

## Running the Model

```sh
python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl
```

## Output Format

```jsonl
{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 12, "objects": ["person", "laptop"], "people":
2}
{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 13, "objects": [], "people": 0}
{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:5", "error": "could not decode video"}
```

- `video` is the Parquet file name without its folder, a colon, and the row number in that file, counting from 0.
- Second 12 holds the frames whose timestamp is at least 12.0 and below 13.0 seconds, counted from the first decoded frame of the video.
- There is a line for every second up to and including the second that holds the last frame. A second with nothing found has an empty list and "people": 0.
- Object names are exactly `person, car, dog, laptop, cell phone`. They are irrespective of order.

## Installing requirements

Python 3.11. No `apt-get` packages are needed.

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

On Linux this installs the CUDA 12 build of PyTorch and TensorRT 10 (from the PyTorch and NVIDIA package indexes listed in `requirements.txt`).

## Preparatory Commands

Run once, from the repository root, on the machine that will run `run.py` (needs internet and the NVIDIA GPU):

```sh
hf download hf://Ultralytics/YOLO11@bee92e2/yolo11l.pt --local-dir yolo
python build_engine.py
```

`build_engine.py` exports `yolo/yolo11l.pt` to a TensorRT FP16 engine at `yolo/yolo11l.engine`. TensorRT engines only work on the GPU model and TensorRT version they were built with, so build it on the target machine. The engine has dynamic input shapes so frames get the same minimal letterbox as the `.pt` model, and a max batch of `BATCH_SIZE` from `run.py`.

## Running the Model

```sh
python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl
```

On CUDA, `run.py` uses `yolo/yolo11l.engine` if it exists, otherwise `yolo/yolo11l.pt` (FP16). Elsewhere it uses `yolo/yolo11l.pt` in FP32. `--model <file>` overrides this.

Development options: `--max-files N`, `--max-rows N` (videos per file), and `--dev` (one video).

## Checking Correctness

`compare.py` scores a results file against a reference with the three checks below. To check the engine against full-precision PyTorch:

```sh
python run.py --input <folder> --output reference.jsonl --model yolo/yolo11l.pt --max-rows 5
python run.py --input <folder> --output engine.jsonl --max-rows 5
python compare.py reference.jsonl engine.jsonl
```

Note `--model yolo/yolo11l.pt` still runs FP16 on CUDA; for an FP32 reference run it on a machine without CUDA, or temporarily set `quantize=None` in `Predictor.predict`.

# YOLO11l Object Detection in HuggingFace FineVideo Dataset for Alethia AI Take Home Assignment

- Dataset: `data/train-00000-of-01357.parquet` to `data/train-00001-of-01357.parquet` of [FineVideo](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFV/finevideo)
- Detection Model: Ultralytics YOLO11l specifically [yolo11l.pt](https://huggingface.co/Ultralytics/YOLO11/blob/main/yolo11l.pt), download in the preparatory commands.
- Assignment details in AI_Engineering_TakeHome_Brief.pdf

## Installing requirements

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Preparatory Commands

```sh
hf download hf://Ultralytics/YOLO11@bee92e2/yolo11l.pt --local-dir yolo
```

## Running the Model

```sh
python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl
```

## Output Format

```jsonl
{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 12, "objects": ["person", "laptop"], "people":
2}
{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 13, "objects": [], "people": 0}
{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:5", "error": "could not decode video"}
```

- `video` is the Parquet file name without its folder, a colon, and the row number in that file, counting from 0.
- Second 12 holds the frames whose timestamp is at least 12.0 and below 13.0 seconds, counted from the first decoded frame of the video.
- There is a line for every second up to and including the second that holds the last frame. A second with nothing found has an empty list and "people": 0.
- Object names are exactly `person, car, dog, laptop, cell phone`. They are irrespective of order.
- If a video can't be processed at any point, there exists an error message `could not decode video`. earlier seconds are already logged, after failure that video is aborted.

## Detection Criteria

- An object is present in a second if the model finds it in at least half of that second's frames.
- The people count for a second is the median of the number of people found in each frame of that second, rounded down when it falls halfway between two numbers.

## Testing Criteria (as per Alethia)

- Objects must have an F1 score of at least 0.95 against the reference.
- People count must match the reference exactly on at least 85% of seconds.
- People count must be within 1 of the reference on at least 95% of seconds.
- The test set is about 13 hours of FineVideo video in the same Parquet format, Some test files may be damaged or unusual. Total test runtime must be less than 6 hours on NVIDIA RTX 4090 with 24 GB of memory, 32 thread CPU with 64 GB of RAM with Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.11, and an NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 12. Some test files may be damaged or unusual.

content.text:
Everything is built and committed on a new branch, `perf/tensorrt-pipeline`, in 6 small commits. Nothing is merged into `main` yet, which is what gets graded. WRITEUP.md still has your uncommitted edits, and I didn't touch it.

**Correctness checks:** I ran the new pipeline and the old code on the same 3 videos (1,082 seconds), on your Mac with the `.pt` model. The results matched exactly (`compare.py`: F1 1.0, people exact 1.0). The new code passes pyright with no errors.

**Error handling:** I tested a folder of damaged files.
- A garbage mp4, an empty (null) cell and a corrupt Parquet file each get one error line, and the good videos around them still process.
- A video cut in half produces about 10 seconds of results and no error line, because the decoder just sees a shorter video. The reference decoder probably reads it the same way, but I can't confirm that.

## Changes
- **Decoding in a separate thread** ([run.py](run.py)): one thread decodes videos into a bounded queue. The main thread runs YOLO on batches of up to 64 frames, which can span several seconds of one video. Each second is written once all its frames have been scored. A batch never mixes frame sizes: mixed sizes would make Ultralytics pad to a full 640×640 square and drift from the reference. Parquet files are read one row at a time instead of whole.
- **TensorRT build** ([build_engine.py](build_engine.py), in the [README](README.md) preparation step): exports an FP16 engine with dynamic input shapes. A fixed-shape engine would pad every frame to 640×640 instead of the 640×384 the `.pt` model uses, which is the same drift. On CUDA, `run.py` uses the engine if it exists, otherwise the `.pt` model.
- **Typing:** type hints throughout, small typed classes for the queue messages, and runtime type checks where pyarrow and Ultralytics data comes in. Pyright's strict mode only complains about those two libraries, which ship without type information.
- **`--fp32` flag, plus `--max-files` and `--max-rows`.** `--fp32` gives you a full-precision reference on the GPU machine to compare the engine against.
- **Dependencies:** added TensorRT 10.16 and ONNX for Linux. TensorRT 11 would need NVIDIA's model-optimizer package to build FP16, so I stayed on 10. Also added `huggingface-hub`, because without it the README's `hf download` preparation command would fail on the grader's fresh VM. I ran that command and it downloads the same weights file you have.

## Tuning batches at runtime
It's possible but not worth it. Trying several batch sizes at startup would spend graded time, and the engine's largest batch is fixed when it's built anyway. Pick `BATCH_SIZE` once on a 4090 instead: try 32, 64 and 128, rebuilding the engine each time, and keep the fastest. That's the only constant to change. Partial batches at the end of a video or a size change still run fine.

## Not tested — needs a rented 4090
I couldn't run any of these on your Mac:
1. `pip install -r requirements.txt` on Ubuntu with Python 3.11. A dry run that simulates Linux resolves correctly, but that isn't a real install.
2. `python build_engine.py` actually building the engine.
3. Accuracy of the engine against the full-precision reference, using the three commands in the README's "Checking Correctness" section.
4. Real speed. On the Mac it's unchanged at 57.4s for the 209s clip because the Mac's GPU is the limit; the gains only show up on CUDA.

Once those pass, merge the branch into `main`.

content.text:
The requirements resolve for Linux on Python 3.11 and 3.12 (74 packages); only 3.10 fails. So the file itself looks fine. The traceback alone doesn't say why torch is missing. There are two likely causes:

1. **`pip install` failed partway.** pip works out all the versions before installing anything, so if it fails at that stage nothing gets installed. If Kaggle runs Python 3.10, it fails exactly that way: `av==18.1.1` requires Python 3.11 or newer. The error would be in the pip output, above where you looked.
2. **`pip` and `python` are different interpreters.** For example, the packages went into a virtual environment but `build_engine.py` ran with the system Python, or the reverse. Kaggle's own Python normally comes with torch, so a missing torch points to a fresh virtual environment, or to running `build_engine.py` with a different Python than the one `pip` installed into.

Run this in the same terminal or notebook and paste the output:

```sh
python --version
which python pip
pip --version
pip install -r requirements.txt 2>&1 | tail -40
```

Using `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` avoids cause 2, because it installs into the same Python that will run the scripts.

Two things to know about testing on Kaggle:
- An engine built on a T4 only works on a T4. That's fine, because the grader builds its own engine during the preparation step.
- I haven't checked whether TensorRT 10.16 still supports the T4. If the install succeeds but `build_engine.py` fails with an error about an unsupported GPU or compute capability, that's the cause, and I'll pick a TensorRT version that supports it.

content.text:
This log shows Python 3.11 being set up, but not the `pip install -r requirements.txt` step, so I still can't see why that failed. The setup itself explains the missing torch, though:

- `update-alternatives` repointed `python3` at a brand-new Python 3.11 from the deadsnakes package archive. Kaggle's preinstalled torch belongs to its original Python, so the new 3.11 starts with no packages at all.
- Packages then have to be installed into that bare system 3.11, which conflicts with the Debian-managed packages already there. That's the `Cannot uninstall packaging 24.0 ... installed by debian` error. If `pip install -r requirements.txt` needs to upgrade any of those packages, it hits the same error and stops before installing torch.

Use a virtual environment instead. That's also exactly what the grader does: a fresh VM, a new virtual environment, then `pip install -r requirements.txt`. In a Kaggle notebook each `!` line runs in its own shell, so `source activate` won't carry over; call the environment's programs by path:

```sh
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && python3.11 -m venv .venv
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -U pip
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt 2>&1 | tail -40
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && .venv/bin/python -c "import torch, tensorrt; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), tensorrt.__version__)"
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && .venv/bin/hf download hf://Ultralytics/YOLO11@bee92e2/yolo11l.pt --local-dir yolo
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && .venv/bin/python build_engine.py
```

If the 4th line prints `2.14.1+cu126 True 10.16.1.11`, the install works. A real pip install on Linux was the main thing I couldn't test on your Mac. If any line fails, paste its output.

content.text:
These are probably not fatal. While building, TensorRT tries several kernel options ("tactics") for each layer. When one needs more GPU memory than is free, it logs this error and skips that option. The build usually continues and finishes with the options that fit.

Check the end of the output:
- If it ends with `Built yolo/yolo11l.engine`, the engine is fine. On a T4 it may be slightly slower than ideal, but the results are not affected.
- If it ends with a traceback or `failed`, paste the last 20 or so lines.

The memory requests are this large (10 GB per option) because Ultralytics sizes a dynamic engine for batch 64 at up to **1280×1280**, twice the input size. That's hardcoded in its exporter (`max_shape = 2 × imgsz`). We never send frames bigger than 640, so most of that headroom is wasted. A T4 has 16 GB. The 4090 has 24 GB, so it should hit this much less.

If the build does fail on the T4, there are two fixes:
1. **For Kaggle only:** temporarily set `BATCH_SIZE = 32` in [run.py](run.py#L35) and rebuild. That halves the largest memory request. Leave 64 in what you commit.
2. **Proper fix:** build the engine with TensorRT directly, capped at 640×640. That means less memory and a faster build, but it replaces Ultralytics' export with about 40 lines of our own code. I'd only do it if the build also struggles on a 4090.

That depends on which step is running.

**If it's `build_engine.py`, this is normal.** A TensorRT build times many kernel options for every layer at the largest batch (64 frames at 640×640). On a T4, a model the size of YOLO11l can take tens of minutes. The graph shows exactly that: GPU 0 at 100%, and one CPU core (101%) driving it. The grader runs this step during preparation, which isn't timed, so build speed doesn't affect your score. Let it finish. An engine built on a T4 only works on a T4, so this build is only for testing on Kaggle.

**If it's `run.py`, I need numbers.** Send the `Total processing time` and the length of the video (or `--dev`, which is the 209s clip). Without TensorRT on a T4, the `.pt` model in FP16 runs at very roughly 50–100 frames per second, so the 4,994-frame clip would take about 1–1.5 minutes. The 4090 is several times faster than a T4, so time on Kaggle doesn't tell you much about the grader's time.

The second T4 sitting at 0% is expected. `run.py` uses one GPU, and the grader's machine has a single 4090. Splitting work across two GPUs would only help on Kaggle.

That's about what a T4 can do with the plain `.pt` model, not a bug. `Using yolo/yolo11l.pt` means the TensorRT engine wasn't used: either `yolo/yolo11l.engine` doesn't exist yet because the build hadn't finished or failed, or this run started before it was built. I'm assuming "per file" means per video. The `--dev` clip is 209s, or 4,994 frames, so "over a minute" is under ~80 frames per second. That's in line with YOLO11l in FP16 PyTorch on a T4.

What it means for grading, roughly (the 4090 figures are estimates, not measurements):

| | Speed | Test set, 13h (~1.1M frames) |
|---|---|---|
| T4, `.pt` FP16 | ~75 fps (what you're seeing) | ~4h |
| 4090, `.pt` FP16 | ~3–4× a T4 | ~1–1.5h |
| 4090, TensorRT FP16 | faster again | under 1h |

So even now it's well inside the 6h limit on the grader's 4090.

To confirm where the time goes on the T4, run this from the repo directory and paste the output:

```sh
!cd /kaggle/working/alethia_yolo11l_object_detection && .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import io, time, av, pyarrow.parquet as pq
from run import Predictor, BATCH_SIZE, to_bgr, default_model
model = default_model("0"); print("model", model)
b = pq.ParquetFile("finevideo/data/train-00000-of-01357.parquet").read_row_group(0, columns=["mp4"]).column(0)[0].as_py()
c = av.open(io.BytesIO(b)); c.streams.video[0].thread_type = "AUTO"
t = time.time(); imgs = [to_bgr(f) for _, f in zip(range(1024), c.decode(video=0))]
print(f"decode+convert: {len(imgs)/(time.time()-t):.0f} fps")
p = Predictor(model, "0", fp16=True); p.predict(imgs[:BATCH_SIZE])  # warm-up
r = p.model.predict(imgs[:BATCH_SIZE], imgsz=640, conf=0.4, classes=p.class_ids, quantize=16, verbose=False, device="0")
print({k: f"{v:.1f} ms/frame" for k, v in r[0].speed.items()})
t = time.time()
for i in range(0, len(imgs), BATCH_SIZE): p.predict(imgs[i:i+BATCH_SIZE])
print(f"predict: {len(imgs)/(time.time()-t):.0f} fps")
EOF
```

Adjust the path if your Parquet files aren't under `finevideo/data`.

How to read the result:
- If decode+convert is several hundred fps or more, decoding isn't the bottleneck.
- If inference is most of each frame's milliseconds, the GPU is the limit, and TensorRT is the fix.
- If preprocess or postprocess is large, the CPU side of Ultralytics is the limit, and I'd move resizing onto the GPU next.

Also check how `build_engine.py` ended. Once `yolo/yolo11l.engine` exists, rerun `--dev`: it should print `Using yolo/yolo11l.engine on device 0`.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. - The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
